title: The preventive effect of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) on Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) epoxidation and the potential against liver cancer carcinogenesis at the initiation

sections.abstract: <jats:p> It is well established that Aflatoxin B <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> (AFB <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> ), a potent liver carcinogen, requires activation by epoxidation either by microsomal P450 enzymes or by the versatile epoxide‐forming oxidant dimethyldioxirane (DMDO). After activation, it is able to inhibit nuclear RNA synthesis and to bind DNA forming DNA adducts. Since DNA adducts can cause mutation, and mutation is the molecular basis for the initiation of carcinogenesis, this is believed to be the molecular mechanism for AFB <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> epoxide to initiation liver cancer carcinogenesis. Based on this insight, a method to screen chemopreventive agents against liver cancer, at the initiation, was developed. This report is to examine the transcriptional and DNA binding properties of EPA and DHA, and the preventive effect on B <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> epoxidation. We found that both EPA and DHA were able to strongly prevent the formation of E <jats:sub>2</jats:sub> epoxide as reflected by the loss of the ability of B <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> to inhibit nuclear RNA synthesis. Additionally, we found that EPA and DHA were able to prevent the binding of [ <jats:sup>3</jats:sup> H]labeled B <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> to DNA. This preventive effect of EPA and DHA on the binding of B <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> to DNA was further confirmed when liver microsomes were used for the activation. We believe that this is the first report on the transcriptional and DNA binding properties of EPA and DHA, and their inhibitory effect on the formation of B <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> epoxide. As a dietary supplement, EPA and DHA may have the potential to prevent B <jats:sub>1</jats:sub> induced liver cancer carcinogenesis at the initiation </jats:p> <jats:p>[This work was partially supported by an Excel Academic Award from SwedishAmerican Hospital].</jats:p>
